newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police smash child pornography ring.
newsitem.headline: German police smash child pornography ring.

text.p: German police said on Tuesday they had smashed a child pornography ring and arrested three men on suspicion of abusing children and using them in pornographic material including 2,000 videos and 50,000 photographs.
Police said the three men, aged 25, 46 and 52, were suspected of persuading children to perform sexual acts and then photographing them.
In a letter to a friend, one of the men boasted he had killed an eight-year-old girl several years ago.

Another of the men wrote to a convicted child murderer in a psychiatric institution, and said he wanted to set up a torture chamber on a farm, where he wanted to kill two boys and two girls during a sex orgy.
It was not yet clear if either of these events had actually taken place, police added.
The leader of the ring, whom police believe was the head of a media marketing company in Berlin, was recently detained in Colombia and extradited to Germany.

The ring was uncovered after a 15-year-old boy reported the 25-year-old man to police following an argument about sexual abuse. The man was a homosexual owner of a photographic shop in the southern town of Nuremberg, police said.
In a separate investigation border police said they had detained a 32-year-old man travelling into Germany from the Czech Republic, on suspicion of sexually abusing a four-year-old boy.
Germany has been at the forefront of efforts to stamp out the distribution of child pornography on the global Internet computer network.
In January German police detained a man and a woman accused of using an on-line service to offer children for sado-masochistic sex.
